injury_note: Jerome (back) won't play in Saturday's game versus Sacramento, Chris Herrington of The Daily Memphian.
injury_news: Jerome has been battling a nagging back injury, though it will finally force him to miss his first game of the 2026-27 campaign. With Scotty Pippen (back) also sidelined, Cam Spencer is the favorite to start at the one.

injury_note: Injury/Illness - Left Foot/Heel Injury Management
injury_news: Williams has missed the past two games for the Lakers, and with Sunday's game being the first of a back-to-back, he might need to spend one more game on the inactive list. If he's out again, Quentin Grimes will help fill his minutes.

injury_note: Injury/Illness - Low Back Soreness
injury_news: Toppin sat out Friday's 145-125 loss to the Heat due to the back issue, and with Sunday's game being the first of a back-to-back set, he may need to spend at least one more game on the sidelines. If he's out, Jarace Walker and Kobe Brown would likely see a bump in minutes.

injury_note: Injury/Illness - Right Knee Contusion /Bone Bruise
injury_news: Suggs suffered the injury during Sunday's win over the Knicks when his right knee buckled following a layup attempt. Fortunately, further testing revealed no major structural damage, though the 25-year-old will miss at least two weeks before being re-evaluated. Anthony Black and Jase Richardson could see increased opportunities in Orlando's backcourt during Suggs' absence.

injury_note: Murray (personal) won't play in Saturday's game against the Hawks, Jim Eichenhofer of the Pelicans' official site reports.
injury_news: Murray wasn't on the injury report but won't suit up due to the birth of his son. With Murray sidelined, Bennedict Mathurin could enter the starting lineup, with Jeremiah Fears operating as the primary ballhandler.

injury_note: Williams (leg) underwent successful surgery Wednesday to "address a fractured left fibula and reconstruction of ankle ligaments following a fracture and dislocation." He will be re-evaluated before the end of the regular season, Tim MacMahon of ESPN.com reports.
injury_news: Williams suffered the injury during Sunday's meeting with the Clippers and was taken off the court on a stretcher. It's unknown when the 25-year-old will be cleared to return, though the Thunder will presumably be overly cautious moving forward. Williams, who signed a five-year extension in July of 2025, has had a productive career, averaging 17.9 points, 4.6 rebounds, 4.4 assists and 1.3 steals over 30.9 minutes per contest. However, after playing at least 69 regular-season games in his first three years in the league, he has appeared in just 36 in the last two seasons combined. With the Thunder having one of the deepest rosters in the NBA, the team may look for more minutes from Jared McCain, Jaylin Williams, and Kenrich Williams for the remainder of the 2026-27 campaign.

injury_note: Embiid (foot) is out for Saturday's game in Charlotte.
injury_news: It's the second night of a back-to-back set, so Embiid will get hit with a maintenance day. Adem Bona will have the opportunity to start Saturday with Embiid inactive.

news_headline: Without injured Brown, 76ers outlast Knicks in NBA Cup Group Play

injury_note: Injury/Illness - Left Knee Tendinitis
injury_news: Santos is expected to continue to push through the pain with his knee issue. He's averaging 7.8 points, 4.2 rebounds and 1.4 assists per game this season.

injury_note: Rest
injury_news: Robinson has been downgraded from questionable to out and will miss the first half of Boston's upcoming back-to-back set. He'll likely be able to suit up Monday in Houston.

news_headline: Victor Wembanyama's Halloween costume trend returns with 'The Witcher' look

injury_note: Injury/Illness - Bilateral Low Back Injury Management
injury_news: Green will sit out the first leg of this back-to-back set, but he should return for Monday's game against the Suns. Graham Ike, Al Horford and Charles Bassey will help pick up the slack with Green inactive Sunday.

injury_note: Holmgren underwent a biological treatment Friday to address a small patellar tendon tear and will miss at least 8-10 weeks, Nick Crain of Slam reports.
injury_news: This is another massive blow to an Oklahoma City squad that's already set to be without Jalen Williams (leg) and Cason Wallace (shoulder) for most, if not all, of the season. With Holmgren sidelined, Kenrich Williams, Jaylin Williams and Aday Mara are all candidates to see increased playing time. Two-way player Brooks Barnhizer could also see more minutes.

injury_note: Johnson (ankle) did not return to Saturday's 121-99 loss to the Pelicans. He finished with 13 points (5-11 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 2-2 FT), seven rebounds, four assists and one block over 28 minutes.
injury_news: Johnson was on the court for the final seconds of the third quarter but didn't see the floor for the entire fourth. The Hawks were facing a large deficit, so the decision to keep him sidelined for the final quarter may have been a precautionary measure. Nevertheless, Johnson's injury status is worth monitoring heading into the Hawks' next game, which takes place Monday against the Pacers. If he were to miss time, then Aaron Wiggins and Luguentz Dort would likely be the top candidates to enter Atlanta's starting lineup.

injury_note: Caruso (ankle) is expected to miss time due to an ankle sprain, Clemente Almanza of USA Today reports.
injury_news: With Caruso already ruled out for Wednesday's game in Dallas due to an ankle sprain, it sounds like the veteran forward could remain sidelined beyond a one-game absence. That would leave Oklahoma City without one of its key rotation wings for at least the near term, which could force Jared McCain into a big role for the banged-up Thunder.

injury_note: James (back) has been ruled out for Saturday's meeting in Charlotte.
injury_news: James will rest on the second leg of a back-to-back set, but he should return for Monday's game against the Bulls. Dean Wade and Justin Edwards should see a bump in minutes with James inactive, while Tyrese Maxey figures to see a sizeable uptick in usage.

injury_note: Surgery Injury/Illness - Left Hamstring Strain
injury_news: Given the tricky nature of hamstring injuries, the Pacers will likely take their time bringing Haliburton back to the court, so don't be surprised if his absence extends beyond this two-week window. Andrew Nembhard (neck) and Pascal Siakam should each get a usage bump as they take over more of the playmaking duties sans Haliburton and there will be more minutes available for Quenton Jackson.

injury_note: Edwards underwent a successful arthroscopic procedure on his right knee Thursday, the Timberwolves announced.
injury_news: Edwards underwent debridement surgery in Minnesota, though the team did not provide a timetable for his return. The star guard is expected to make a full recovery, with additional updates coming as he progresses through rehabilitation. Based on previous reporting from ESPN's Shams Charania, Edwards could miss up to two months. Edwards was off to a scorching start this season, averaging 33.3 points, 4.8 rebounds, 3.5 assists and 2.0 steals across four appearances.
news_headline: Timberwolves' Anthony Edwards undergoes successful knee scope

injury_note: Champagnie (foot) is expected to miss several months, per Josh Robbins of The Athletic.
injury_news: The forward underwent surgery Wednesday to address a fractured foot, and the Wizards hope Champagnie will be ready to return at some time around the All-Star break in February. The likes of Bilal Coulibaly, Tre Johnson and Bub Carrington will all be asked to help pick up the slack for the foreseeable future.

injury_note: Post (ankle) has been ruled out for Saturday's game versus Sacramento, Chris Herrington of The Daily Memphian reports.
injury_news: Post was listed as doubtful, and now we have official confirmation that he'll be on the inactive list Saturday night. His minutes will likely be divvied up amongst Isaiah Stewart and Taylor Hendricks.

injury_note: Gobert (back) is out for Saturday's game against the Spurs, Dane Moore of 'The Dane Moore NBA Podcast' reports.
injury_news: Gobert will miss his first game of the season Saturday, which could result in Joan Beringer getting the start and Trey Lyles could see a bump in minutes. For now, Gobert should be considered questionable for Monday's meeting with Milwaukee.

injury_note: Morant has been diagnosed with a Grade 2 left hamstring strain and is expected to miss four weeks, Portland announced Friday.
injury_news: Morant left Thursday's game early with a hamstring injury, which has since been revealed to be a strain that will result in a monthlong absence. The star guard leaves a major void in the Trail Blazers' starting backcourt, one that figures to be filled by Jrue Holiday for the foreseeable future.
news_headline: Ja Morant out at least 4 weeks with hamstring strain suffered against Grizzlies

injury_note: Injury/Illness - Right Knee Injury Management
injury_news: Sunday's game will be the first of a back-to-back set, so Curry will receive a maintenance day, but he should return for Monday's meeting with the Suns. De'Anthony Melton could draw the start sans Curry, and Brandin Podziemski will be more involved in the offense.

injury_note: Sheppard (back) is out for Saturday's game against the Thunder.
injury_news: This will be Sheppard's second straight game on the sidelines, and for now, he should be viewed as questionable for Monday's game against the Celtics. Fred VanVleet (knee) will join Sheppard on the inactive list for Saturday's game, paving the way for Marcus Smart to start.

injury_note: Tyson (ankle) has been ruled out for Saturday's game against the Bucks.
injury_news: Tyson is dealing with a right ankle sprain and won't suit up Saturday, with his next chance to play coming Monday against the Thunder. With the 23-year-old forward sidelined, Mario Hezonja, Sam Merrill and Meleek Thomas (foot) are candidates for increased playing time.

injury_note: Injury/Illness - Right Bone Bruise
injury_news: Brooklyn's decision keeps Demin under contract through the 2027-28 campaign as the organization continues investing in its young backcourt. The move provides additional long-term stability but doesn't directly impact his immediate fantasy outlook. Demin is currently dealing with a right leg bone bruise and is scheduled to be re-evaluated in one week.

injury_note: Jackson has been diagnosed with a torn MCL in his right knee and will be sidelined for 6-to-8 weeks, per Shams Charania of ESPN.
injury_news: Jackson sustained the injury early in Monday's loss to Memphis, and he's now expected to miss at least a month and a half of action. The star big man's absence creates a major void in the Utah lineup, one that is likely to be filled by a timeshare of Jaxson Hayes (shoulder), Kyle Filipowski and Mo Bamba. The Jazz could also shift Lauri Markkanen (wrist), when healthy, to the center spot at times, perhaps allowing Ace Bailey to spend more time at power forward.

injury_note: Pippen (back) has been ruled out for Saturday's game against the Kings, Chris Herrington of The Daily Memphian reports.
injury_news: Pippen is working through a back injury and will end up missing his first game of the regular season. He is averaging 16.0 minutes per game off the bench, and that playing time will be absorbed by Cam Spencer, GG Jackson and Jerami Grant. Pippen's next opportunity to play is Monday against the Pelicans.

injury_note: VanVleet (knee) won't play Saturday against the Thunder.
injury_news: It's the second night of a back-to-back set, so VanVleet will receive his standard maintenance day, but he should return for Monday's meeting with the Celtics. Reed Sheppard (back) is also out for Saturday's game, so Marcus Smart could draw the start at point guard, and Amen Thompson should see some increased playmaking responsibilities.

news_headline: Golden State Warriors' Charles Bassey reflects on 'long, adverse' NBA journey thanks to injuries

injury_note: Joe (hip) has been ruled out for Friday's game against the Nets.
injury_news: Joe will miss a third straight game due to a right hip contusion, and his next chance to return will come Monday at Charlotte. With the 27-year-old swingman sidelined, Kevin Huerter, Javonte Green and Ronald Holland are candidates to see increased burn.

injury_note: Landale (hip) won't return to Saturday's game against the Pelicans.
injury_news: Landale only logged one minute Saturday before exiting the contest. His next opportunity to get back on the floor will come Monday versus Indiana. In the meantime, Asa Newell should see more playing time behind Onyeka Okongwu.

injury_note: Injury/Illness - Left Hamstring Strain
injury_news: Nesmith didn't play in the 123-120 loss to New Orleans on Opening Night but has played in each of the Pacers' last five contests. Although he could see limited action while he continues to work his way back from the left hamstring strain, he will likely be out there Sunday, barring a setback.

injury_note: Poole (ankle) has been ruled out for Saturday's game against the Hawks.
injury_news: Poole will miss a second straight game due to a sprained left ankle. His next chance to suit up will come Monday at Memphis. Bennedict Mathurin and Herbert Jones are candidates for increased playing time in Poole's absence.

injury_note: Injury/Illness - Left Ankle Sprain
injury_news: This will be Zubac's fourth consecutive game on the sidelines, which should result in another start for Jay Huff and extended minutes for Larry Nance. Zubac's next chance to play will come Monday against the Hawks.

injury_note: Wallace underwent surgery Friday to repair a torn labrum in his left shoulder and will be re-evaluated before the end of the regular season, Clemente Almanza of USA Today reports.
injury_news: Wallace is expected to miss most, if not all, of the season. However, there's still a chance he will return late in the campaign after sustaining the shoulder injury in Sunday's win over the Clippers. With Jalen Williams (leg) also set to be re-evaluated before the end of the regular season, Alex Caruso (ankle) should see significant playing time once cleared to return. In the meantime, Jared McCain, Bennett Stirtz and Josh Dix are expected to see increased burn.

injury_note: Injury/Illness - Back, Injury Management
injury_news: Brown will skip the first leg of this upcoming back-to-back set, but he should return for Monday's game in New York. With Brown inactive, there will be more minutes available for Nolan Traore, Terance Mann and Keon Ellis.

injury_note: Head coach Dusty May said Friday that de Larrea (knee) will be re-evaluated next week, Noah Weber of TheSmokingCuban.com reports.
injury_news: De Larrea sprained his right knee in Monday's win over Miami and is without a definitive timetable for a return to action. However, his absence shouldn't cause any significant waves in the rotation.
